title: Observer fanout with tenant credit bucketing and non-blocking canary taps
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a non-blocking observer fanout that duplicates live requests to canary/analysis targets while enforcing per-tenant credit buckets, differential sampling, and automatic quiesce/rollback triggers for cost or error spikes. This ticket designs and implements the core policy and runtime plumbing so product teams can run long-running A/B tests and canaries without risking runaway cost or cross-tenant interference.

Background: Current experimental tap/replication pipelines either risk blowing tenant budgets during surges or introduce tail latency when the duplication path is synchronous. We need a lightweight observer that: duplicates requests asynchronously, attributes cost to tenant-level buckets, supports configurable sampling strategies, isolates downstream tenant artifacts (credentials/headers), and can stop forwarding automatically based on policy thresholds or canary signals.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI for Console controls (separate PM/UX work) and does not cover on-prem installation packaging for private deployments (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Observer service duplicates requests asynchronously without adding >3ms median p95 to production request paths when running at 10k RPS in staging
Per-tenant credit bucket created and decremented for each duplicated request; tenants can set monthly and spare-credit budgets
Configurable sampling strategies available: uniform, stratified-by-customer, header-based, rate-limited burst allowance
Automatic quiesce policy that pauses forwarding when tenant bucket falls below threshold or duplication-induced error rate increase >2% over baseline
End-to-end attribution logs emitted to billing pipeline and Console telemetry for token counts and egress costs
Non-blocking contract: production request success/failure semantics unchanged even if observer path is slow or failing
E2E tests and load test harness demonstrating cost containment and isolation on multi-tenant scenarios
technical_plan: Add lightweight observer sidecar in gateway outbound path to fork a copy of request into an internal 'observer-queue' (async, best-effort)
Implement tenant credit-bucketer microservice with in-memory fast-path cache and persistent ledger writes to billing store; expose token-level accounting API
Sampling engine: pluggable scheduler supporting uniform, stratified, header-based and adaptive burst windows with tenant override rules
Isolation transform pipeline to strip/rotate any sensitive headers, attach per-tenant ephemeral creds where required, and tag copies with canary context metadata
Quiesce & rollback hooks: metrics-based rule engine that monitors observer-derived errors & cost and triggers pause/alert; exposes webhooks for Console-driven rollback
Safe-fallback: when observer queue is full or bucket depleted, drop copies and emit drop_reason metric; do NOT block upstream paths
Telemetry: emit token counts, bytes, sampling decisions, drop reasons, and latency histograms to observability with tenant tag keys
Integration: wire billing attribution to existing billing pipeline (events topic) with per-copy charge metadata; add reconciler to detect ledger drift
tasks: Design API for tenant credit-bucketer and ledger schema (task: API contract + migration plan)
Implement observer sidecar insertion point in gRPC/HTTP gateway and ensure non-blocking behavior
Build sampling engine and unit tests for strategies
Implement isolation transform chain to sanitize copies
Add quiesce rule engine and connect to alerting + webhook
Instrument telemetry and create Console telemetry dashboard prototype (backend only)
E2E load tests and chaos test (simulate queue pressure, bucket exhaustion, downstream errors)
Create integration with billing events topic and reconciler job
